excerpts.text: The SI (2019) states that amount of substance is proportional to the number of entities in a sample, and the reciprocal of the proportionality factor is called the Avogadro constant _N_ A.

We contend that (i) 1 mol of all samples contains a fixed number of entities, which the SI calls the Avogadro number, (ii) amount of substance is a value on the scale of measurement defined by the mole, and (iii) the 2019 SI Avogadro number (6.022 140 76×10 23) is the established value of the 1970 SI Avogadro number, which is a constant physical quantity.

excerpts.text: Relative atomic masses Metrologia Amount of substance and the mole in the SI Bernd Güttler1, Horst Bettin1, Richard J C Brown2 , Richard S Davis3 , Zoltan Mester4 , Martin J T Milton3 , Axel Pramann1 , Olaf Rienitz1 , Robert D Vocke5 and Robert I Wielgosz3 1 Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt (PTB), Bundesallee 100, 38116 Braunschweig, Germany 2 National Physical Laboratory (NPL), Hampton Road, Teddington, Middlesex, TW11 0LW, United Kingdom 3 Bureau International des Poids et Mesures (BIPM), Pavillon de Breteuil, F-92312 Sèvres CEDEX, France 4 National Research Council Canada (NRC), 1200 Montreal Road, Ottawa, Ontario K1A 0R6, Canada 5 National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), 100 Bureau Drive, Gaithersburg, MD 20899, United States of America E-mail: bernd.guettler@ptb.de Received 2 February 2019, revised 24 April 2019 Accepted for publication 7 May 2019 Published 3 June 2019 Abstract Following the revision of the International System of Units (SI), that takes effect on 20 May 2019, the unit mole is defined by using a fixed number of elementary entities. This number is the fixed numerical value of the Avogadro constant, which is the defining constant of the unit mole.
